correctness.rationale: A nonzero entry of the 12x11 C_phi(m,n) rank test requires an ordered support pair with additive difference m and multiplicative quotient n. For |S|<=3 there are at most six ordered pairs. For |S|=4, rank 11 requires >=11 distinct nonzero additive differences, but they form an even set, hence all 12 and each ordered difference occurs exactly once: a planar (13,4,1) difference set. Exhaustive direct Python enumeration over all C(13,4)=715 4-subsets found 52 perfect sets, precisely affine translates/scalings of D={0,1,3,9}; each admissible translation has at most 9 nonidentity multiplicative ratios and so cannot yield column rank 11. For the five-site witness (1,2,3,4,11) with weights (1,2,4,8,16), its dominant coefficient makes all multiplicative chars of |phi|² nonzero; independently computed exact 11x11 minor determinant -2^43, so the Bartusel–Führ–Oussa criterion yields full complex 12x12 matrix recovery. Reviewed an independent finite-field 156x144 rank-mod-53 certificate in the supplied source: since 10 has order 13 mod53 it legitimately certifies a characteristic-zero nonzero maximal minor. Finite exhaustive scope is all p=13, not extrapolation.
residual_risks: The result is prime=13 and full matrix recovery, not a universal prime-field support threshold or the possibly weaker rank-one phase retrieval minimum.
The published BFO criterion is an explicit mathematical input; its proof is not re-established independently in this record.
